refusal.label: #sep-2026-sprint
refusal.text:
On T2: the experimentation platform is the part of our stack I know least about — the definitions layer, the stats engine, how it maps to what the steering group actually needs to decide. I've done staged rollouts before and I know where they break, but I've never been near this side of the platform. Two weeks on it is the fastest way to close that gap, and the review benefits from having someone who has to learn it rather than someone who already lives in it. That's my reason.

For the meeting: 10:00–10:30 works. The other two conflict with the interview panel and team sync.

Priya, that leaves the rollout's data-science slot on T1 with Matthieu, if you want it.

Rafael — first meeting today: 10:15, 30 min, work for you?

refusal.label: #sep-2026-sprint
refusal.text:
Taking T2 — the platform review. The board already has me on it; here's the case written down properly, since that's the ask.

Concrete fit: this review turns on when a number can be trusted and when it can't, and that's the quarter I've had. The session table double-firing since the new SDK — everything after the 9th inflated until we deduped on the way in. The migration backfill that quietly made every cohort chart with a January in it wrong. The churn-label refresh — the 90-day window, the win-back cases, what counts as a churned account at all. "What is this platform fit to decide" is the same muscle as "what counts as a churned account," and I've been exercising it on live data all month. I'd rather the go/no-go write-up came from someone who's been burned by all three.

First meeting: 10:00–10:30 today — your first slot works, I'm out of standup at 10:00. Sending the calendar invite now; shout if you'd rather a different one.
